name: Processor D
justification: Our baseline benchmarks on Processor A and Processor B revealed that the primary bottleneck in simulating periodic ring Hamiltonians is topological mismatch. Processor A is a 5-qubit tree lacking any 4-cycle, which forces the SABRE transpiler to insert 11 routing SWAP gates (33 additional CX gates and depth 100), severely degrading fidelity. Processor B contains cycles but has higher average path length across its 9 qubits. Processor D resolves this bottleneck by implementing a 9-qubit cubic hypercube hybrid topology featuring an inner 4-qubit cycle (0,1,2,3) connected directly to a parallel 4-qubit cycle (4,5,6,7) via chordal bus lines, coupled to an ancillary readout port node 8. This eliminates 100% of routing SWAP gates for the 4-spin ring TFIM Hamiltonian while maintaining a strictly planar maximum node degree of 4. We assume standard superconducting transmon error rates (p1=0.001, p2=0.005, readout=0.01) matching the official noise specification. The design accepts the trade-off of limiting node degree to 4 to prevent microwave crosstalk and frequency crowding, requiring multi-hop routing for non-adjacent outer-ring interactions.
